SPEC:
load(defaults, file_values, env) builds a settings dict with exactly the keys of defaults. For each key the value comes from env (a dict keyed by the key in upper case, whose values are strings) when present, else from file_values when present, else from defaults. Values from file_values are already typed and are used as they are. A value from env is converted by coerce(value, like) in coerce.py to the type of the default: for a bool default, true, yes, on, and 1 in any letter case mean True, and false, no, off, and 0 mean False, and anything else raises ValueError; for an int default, int(value); for a str default, the string unchanged. Keys in env or file_values that are not in defaults are ignored. The bug is not necessarily in mod.py. Examples are Python. load({'port': 80}, {}, {'PORT': '8080'}) is {'port': 8080}. load({'debug': False}, {}, {'DEBUG': 'yes'}) is {'debug': True}. load({'debug': True}, {}, {'DEBUG': 'FALSE'}) is {'debug': False}. load({'debug': True}, {'debug': False}, {}) is {'debug': False}. load({'name': 'a'}, {'name': 'b'}, {'NAME': 'c'}) is {'name': 'c'}. load({'debug': False}, {}, {'DEBUG': 'maybe'}) raises ValueError.
